fields.name: tile5b
fields.fieldText:
DETERMINING THE INBOUND FAX ISSUE USING THE SESSION LOG TOOL If the customer is experiencing issues receiving faxes, the Session Log tool will tell you the reason why inbound faxes are failing.
  • Ask the customer the phone number where the faxes are coming from as well as the date and time of when they were sent.
  • Search for that number using the Session Log tool.
  • NOTE: The Session Log tool shows all logs in Pacific Time. If you need help converting the time, please use available online tools such as:
    • Time Difference Calculator
    • Time Zone Converter
    Below are the components to look for when analyzing inbound faxing issues:
  • Blue: - Session Type
    • This indicates how the transmission was processed by the system.
    • Inbound fax indicates that the fax machine of the sender has successfully reached the RingCentral number and the call was processed as a fax transmission.
    • Caller indicates that the fax machine of the sender reached the RingCentral number but the call was not processed as a fax transmission.
  • Red: - Sender information
    • This indicates the number of the sender. The phone number is under Caller ID.
  • Yellow: - Receiving number
    • This indicates the RingCentral number the sender has sent the fax to.
  • Green: - Receiving user extension
    • This indicates the user extension where the fax was processed.
    • NOTE: Fax only accounts do not have user extensions hence this field is blank
  • Purple: - Inbound fax status
    • Results under Action or PPhone/Connect wlil indicate th results of the fax transmission
The sample above indicates the following facts:
  • The transmission was processed by the system as a fax.
  • The sender's number is 16505393557.
  • The RingCentral number the fax was sent to is 18885735024.
  • The user extension the where the fax was processed is User Extension 0.
  • The inbound fax status shows that the fax was successfully received by 18885735024.

fields.name: tile4f
fields.fieldText: FURTHER ISOLATING THE PROBLEM To further isolate if the problem was indeed caused by RingCentral, ask the customer the number of pages they were expecting to have received but came in partial. If the results showing on the Session Log tool indicate the message: Fax Received, this indicates that the system has correctly proccessed the inbound fax and the fax message should have been delivered to the user extension's mailbox. if the customer is reporting that certain pages are missing, the customer would need to contact the sender and report the issue. A Fax Received status indicate that RingCentral completely received the fax that was transmitted by the sender from start to end. NOTE: Certain fax machine models have a feature to stop and complete the fax transmission if they deem that the quality of the phone line is bad. This is good on the receiver's part as it helps conserve paper and avoid re-printing of already received pages. The fax machine then sends the remaining pages as new faxes until the whole document has been completely sent out. Having this in mind, since the sending fax machine stopped and completed the transmission, RingCentral labels the transmission as: Fax Recieved.

fields.name: tile1
fields.fieldText:
INCOMING FAX TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE This guide will walk you through the proper identification and resolution of a incoming fax issues. Each issue should be handled individually and all information you've gathered must be recorded in the case. PREREQUISITES Before you start following this guide, please ensure that ALL of the following settings are correct:
  • User Extension Status
    • Must be Enabled.
  • Phone number type
    • The phone number type in Admin Interface must be set to Main Number, Dedicated Fax, Voice/Fax, or Fax.
NOTE: In certain conditions, the Main Number could be set as a Voice Only number, It will be best to check the number type of the main number from the online account.
  • Take Messages setting set to Yes
    • The Take Messages setting does not only pertain to voicemail messages received by the user extension. The setting is also applicable to received faxes.
False fax tones (a recorded file of the actual sound of a fax tone) cannot be used as User Greetings
  • In an attempt to mimic the behavior of dedicated fax numbers, false fax tones cannot be used as a User Greeting because it interferes with how RingCentral listens for incoming faxes.
  • Faxes sent to user extensions whose User Greeting is set as false fax tones will not be processed as fax, rather they go in to the user's mailbox as a voicemail.
  • Incoming faxes sent to Analog Telephone Adapters (ATA) are not supported by this guide.
  • Incoming faxes received by a fax machine that is connected to an ATA are not processed by RingCentral's fax server.
  • In this set up, faxes are directly transmitted to the fax machine via the ATA.
  • Check if the account has enough minutes by going through the Admin Interface > Account Info then look for "Used Minutes"
  • Check if the Fax number of the sender not set to block calls/faxes by checking it on the online account first go to Extension of the fax number > Screening greeting and hold music > Blocked Calls
Note: In the event that you encounter a road block when using this guide, please ask assistance from a Team Lead.

Click "Next" to continue

ISSUE IDENTIFICATION Incoming fax issues vary depending on the symptoms customers are reporting. Below are the most common issues being reported and their corresponding symptoms: UNABLE TO RECEIVE FAXES Symptoms:
  • The customer suddenly stopped receiving faxes.
  • Faxes are not coming in and Call Logs show that the result of incoming faxes are Missed or Fax Receipt Error.
  • Faxes are not coming in and Call Logs are not showing any information why the customer failed to receive them.
FAXES ARE PARTIALLY RECEIVED Symptoms:
  • Faxes are being received but the pages are incomplete.
  • Faxes are shown as Partial Receive when viewed from the Call Logs screen.

fields.name: tile9e
fields.fieldText: LIMITATIONS OF FAX OVER IP RingCentral cannot guarantee 100% success rate since faxing over the internet has known limitations. RingCentral uses the T.38 standard for faxing and adheres to the FCC guidelines regarding its use. This standard is interpreted differently by the various carriers and service providers on the public telephone and internet networks. Given this, the T.38 standard cannot be guaranteed on all end to end connections. DETERMINE HOW MANY SENDERS ARE EXPERIENCING ISSUES Eventhough RingCentral does not have full control on how faxes will be transmitted by the sender, RingCentral does it's best to ensure it's compatibility with most modern fax machines. The most is reasonable way to identify where the problem happens, is to determine the amount of senders experiencing issues sending faxes to the RingCentral number. The more failed call samples coming from the different numbers provided by this and other customers, the quicker advanced tiers can isolate and resolve the issue.

SEND A TEST FAX USING THE FAXAGE TOOL If the customer has not been frequently having issues receiving faxes recently, RingCentral will have a difficult time determining where the problem is really happening from. To easily isolate if the problem is indeed coming from RingCentral's end, it will be best to send test faxes to the RingCentral number using a non-RingCentral tool to be able to simulate "real world results". Log in to the FAXAGE tool by going to https://www.faxage.com/login.php and using the following credentials:
  • Username: rctester
  • Company: 21950
  • Password: xcq896
NOTE: This tool is meant for internal use of RingCentral Customer Support. Any usage of the tool outside RingCentral's support may render the account inactive causing problems to other users of the tool. Please be responsible when sending test faxes!
  • Once logged in, click send tab at the top page
  • Select Manually Specify from the dropdown menu then click the arrow beside it.
  • Manually enter the customer's fax number then click the arrow beside it.
  • Select Upload file(s) from the dropdown menu and click the arrow beside it. Leave the other boxes unchecked.
  • Download the 1-page text fax from https://drive.google.com/open?id=0ByTiFAvzfEH5VnNvZ2g0d3p1cFE then save it on your computer.
  • Click Choose Files then select the file that you have just downloaded. Click Add File.
  • Click Send FAX
NOTE: Receiving the fax may take from several seconds to a couple of minutes depending on the amount of queued faxes. Be patient and wait for the results of the test fax.
